newsitem.title: CHINA: China to sack accident-hit coal mine managers.
newsitem.headline: China to sack accident-hit coal mine managers.

text.p: China is to sack managers of coal mines that suffer serious accidents as part of a drive to boost mine safety, the Xinhua Daily Telegraph said on Friday.

Officials would also cut workforces as part of efforts to further reduce coal industry losses, which fell to 600 million yuan ($72 million) in 1996, down 41 percent from 1995, it quoted Minister of Coal Industry Wang Senhao as saying.
China has long sought to reform its coal mines, many of which are small, inefficient and have a poor safety record.
The manager of any mine that suffered an accident in which 10 or more people died would be sacked from now on, the newspaper quoted Wang as saying.

The managers of coal bureaux that suffered two or more accidents that killed 10 or more miners, or which suffered one especially big accident, should also be sacked, Wang said. Coal bureaux are responsible for overseeing mines.
China, the world's largest coal producer, has vowed to streamline and modernise its coal industry by merging major mines into more efficient groups and by boosting exports.
Officials say larger scale mining could also greatly reduce China's high rate of mining deaths and accidents. About 10,000 workers are killed in Chinese mines every year.
